cohort: The study included 446 randomly selected mothers who delivered at public health facilities in the Harari Region, Eastern Ethiopia.
finding: Despite the policy of providing delivery services free of charge, mothers incurred a median out-of-pocket cost of US$ 27.3 for delivery services in public health facilities, with direct non-medical expenses, particularly food-related, accounting for a substantial portion.
mod_finding: Modes of delivery were identified as a significant predictor of the median total cost of delivery services.
